column1: First, what is this magnet?
It's called a rare earth magnet.
It's mostly iron.
Add a little boron... and one special metal, called neodymium.
It's small, but it's very strong.
And in a motor, strength is everything.
Here's why.
A stronger magnet gives you the same push from a smaller motor.
Smaller means lighter.
And lighter means you get more kilometres on one charge.
Makes sense?
That's why the spec sheet says permanent magnet.
Most electric scooters and cars on the road use these magnets in their motors.
And it's not just vehicles.
Remember the buzz in your phone?
Same kind of magnet.
You'll also find it in many wind turbines, and in defence systems.
Now look at this number.
India needs about four thousand tonnes of these magnets a year... and we buy almost all of them from abroad.
And more than eight out of every ten come from one country.
China.
So you're probably thinking — if the sand is ours, why can't we just dig it up and make them?
Let's open that box.
